findings.location: <harness-onion>/architecture/review-record/README.md 'SHAPE beyond the schemas (RR2C1-3)'; <harness-onion>/schemas/review-identity.schema.json runs[].used; <harness-onion>/schemas/review-briefs.schema.json briefs[].version; the date and time patterns of the four schemas; <harness-onion>/scripts/review_record.py _int, _valid_date, _instant
findings.finding: The README claims that on I-JSON values the model refuses SHAPE exactly when a schema rejects, apart from four listed causes. Probe 2 used jsonschema Draft 2020-12 as the tests apply it, without a format checker, over 101 date, time and integer cases in all four forms. It found 20 disagreements. 12 are the declared 'day the month lacks'. 8 are undeclared, all model-only SHAPE and fail-closed. (1) Six are year 0000 in reviewDate, ruling.date (review and oracle identities), launched and finished (both identities) and supersededAt. RFC 3339 and the tightened patterns admit year 0000, but datetime cannot represent it. (2) One is identity runs[].used of 2^53. _int caps at 2^53-1, but this schema member has no maximum, unlike round. (3) One is a registry version of 2^53, for the same reason. The README also says each cause is pinned by a vector marked modelOnly. The I-JSON cause's row (shape-duplicate-member-text) is not so marked, and the exponent form has no row. The practical exposure is nil, but check 4's claim as the README states it still does not hold.
findings.requiredChange: Either add maximum 9007199254740991 to runs[].used and to the registry's version, and exclude year 0000 from the date and time patterns of the schemas and the model, or list these causes in the README's model-only list, each with a vector. Reword 'pinned by a vector marked modelOnly' to match the I-JSON row.

findings.finding: The README and check_merge's docstring both say that a cited record that cannot be read as a round 'counts for nothing', with a refusal only when no series counts. The model refuses the whole merge with NO_HEAD_BOUND_ROUND as soon as any cited record cannot be loaded or lacks a string series and an integer round. Probe 3 M2: a passing PR round 1 plus one unrelated unreadable record gives NO_HEAD_BOUND_ROUND. The vector merge-unreadable-round-number (a passing round 1 plus a round 2.0) follows RR2C1-7's requiredChange and the model, but not the README's words. The model's fail-closed behaviour is the right one; only the text is wrong.
findings.requiredChange: Reword the README and the docstring: a cited record that cannot be read as a round refuses the merge (NO_HEAD_BOUND_ROUND), and a series that fails check_series counts for nothing.

findings.location: <harness-onion>/architecture/review-record/README.md 'Rules (B-3), checked when the registry is loaded'; <harness-onion>/scripts/review_record.py load_registry; vectors.json bases.registry and registries/registry-three-version-chain
findings.finding: The fix adds a sentence to the load-time rule list, where a break is SHAPE: 'a new version gets a new path, so each registered sha256 stays the bytes at its path'. load_registry does not check this. The vectors' base registry has EXAMPLE-002 versions 1 and 2 on one path, and the new row registry-three-version-chain puts version 3 on that same path and expects a clean load (probe 3: 2 versions, 1 distinct path, loads). So the stated rule, the model and the vectors disagree. A brief superseded in place would also break the oracle's every-version binding test (RR2C1-12).
findings.requiredChange: Choose one. Refuse two versions of one chain on one path as SHAPE at load, give the vector versions distinct paths, and add a refusal row. Or move the sentence out of the load-time list, as a convention that the in-suite tests check for the latest version only.

findings.finding: check_series runs check_review on every round, and check_review refuses a PENDING or VOID ruling. Since the fix, check_merge checks every cited round from 1. So a series with a VOID round can never count for a merge: probe 3 M3 (round 1 VOID, round 2 passing) gives NO_HEAD_BOUND_ROUND. check_tree also refuses a published VOID round (T4: RULING). This follows rev 4, but the README does not say how a voided round is replaced.
findings.requiredChange: State how a VOID round is handled, for example by a new series id, or by never publishing a voided round. Or put the question to the monitor.

findings.finding: Both re-stamped identities keep candidateCommit 9f88e824. Their new disclosures say that the scoped follow-up ran against the uncommitted r1 fix work tree on 0bc5dc1a. So the re-stamped oracle file's published-registry case and its PACKET merge cases fail against any earlier commit, 9f88e824 included. This is by reading; I did not run it. The README calls candidateCommit 'the candidate commit the oracle tested'.
